tools.name: seo_audit_page
tools.description: Audit a single page and return prioritised, actionable findings (rule id, severity, message, recommendation, CSS selector, evidence) with a `fix` for each: the exact edits that resolve it, quoting the code to replace (`{{…}}` marks words the author writes). Checks title, meta description, headings, canonical, robots/noindex, viewport/lang, Open Graph/Twitter cards, images, links, hreflang, structured data (JSON-LD/microdata), content quality and the HTTP response. Provide either `url` (live site, staging or http://localhost dev server) or `html` (raw HTML string, e.g. from a template or test render). Set `render: true` to also load the page in headless Chromium and report content that only exists after JavaScript runs (SPA/CSR problems). Set `lighthouse: true` for Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, TBT) and Lighthouse SEO audits; this takes 20-60 seconds. Typical workflow: audit, apply the `fix` of each error and warning in the source code, then re-check with `rules` (the rules you fixed) and `baseline` (the finding ids) to confirm they are fixed and nothing new appeared.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL to fetch and audit.

html.description: Raw HTML to audit instead of fetching a URL.

baseUrl.description: With `html`: the URL the HTML would be served at (used to resolve links and classify them as internal/external).

render.description: Also render with headless Chromium (Playwright) and compare against the server HTML.

lighthouse.description: Also run Lighthouse (performance, SEO, agentic-browsing categories). Slow.

keyword.description: Target keyword/phrase. Enables keyword.* checks (title, H1, body, description, URL, density).

includeInfo.description: Include info-level findings (best practices). Set false to see only errors and warnings.

disableRules.description: Rule ids to skip, e.g. ["twitter.card-missing"]. Use seo_list_rules to see ids.

rules.description: Run only these rule ids, e.g. ["img.alt-missing"] to re-check the findings a fix was for. Use with `baseline`.

baseline.description: The `id` of every finding of the earlier audit. The result then has `baseline`: the ids since fixed, still open and new (a new one may be a problem a fix caused). Re-check with the same options; for a crawl or directory, run both audits with pageDetail full so page findings have ids.

headers.description: Extra request headers, e.g. {"Authorization": "Basic ..."} for staging sites.

format.description: json (default) returns the structured audit; markdown returns a human-readable report.

detail.description: compact trims evidence lists and bulky fields to save tokens (default); full returns everything.

tools.name: seo_crawl_site
tools.description: Crawl internal links from a start URL (default 25 pages, depth 3), audit every HTML page, and run site-wide checks: robots.txt, XML sitemap coverage (missing/noindex/non-canonical/broken URLs), broken internal links with their sources, redirect chains, duplicate titles/descriptions/H1s/content, orphan and deep pages, soft-404 behaviour, http→https and www redirects, hreflang return links. Returns site findings plus `issues` (page findings rolled up by rule with example URLs) and per-page scores. Use seo_audit_page on a specific URL for full per-page detail. Works on http://localhost dev servers; for those set `respectRobots: false` if the dev server serves a blocking robots.txt.

maxDepth.description: Maximum link depth from the start URL.

respectRobots.description: Obey robots.txt disallow rules while crawling.

includeSubdomains.description: Treat subdomains of the start host as internal.

checkExternalLinks.description: Also probe external link targets for 4xx/5xx (slower).

includePatterns.description: Only crawl URLs matching one of these regular expressions.

excludePatterns.description: Skip URLs matching any of these regular expressions.

pageDetail.description: summary: per-page scores/counts only (findings are rolled up in `issues`); full: every finding on every page.

tools.name: seo_audit_directory
tools.description: Audit every .html file in a build output directory (dist/, out/, build/, .output/public) without running a server. Runs all page checks plus directory-level checks: internal links that resolve to no file, sitemap.xml/robots.txt in the output, duplicate titles/descriptions/content, unlinked files. Pass `baseUrl` as the production origin (e.g. https://www.example.com) so absolute links, canonicals and sitemap URLs are classified correctly.

baseUrl.description: Origin the files will be served from.

tools.name: seo_lighthouse
tools.description: Run Google Lighthouse (performance, SEO and agentic-browsing categories) against one URL using a local headless Chrome. Returns Core Web Vitals lab metrics (LCP, CLS, TBT, FCP, Speed Index, TTFB), the top opportunities with estimated savings, failed Lighthouse SEO audits, and findings with thresholds applied. Takes 20-60 seconds. Requires Chrome or Playwright Chromium on this machine.

formFactor.description: Device emulation. Mobile is what Google uses for ranking.

headers.description: Extra request headers (e.g. auth for staging).

format.description: json (default) returns the structured audit; markdown returns a human-readable report.

tools.name: seo_aeo_audit
tools.description: Answer engine optimization audit: can AI answer engines (ChatGPT search, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Copilot, Gemini) reach, quote and trust the content? Checks robots.txt for each AI crawler (search crawlers, answer bots, training bots), Content-Signal lines and the shared `__usage_ai-training` opt-out, /llms.txt, nosnippet/max-snippet/data-nosnippet, Bing's noarchive/nocache for Copilot, noai, content that needs JavaScript, question headings without a direct answer, FAQPage/HowTo markup that the page does not show, article author and dates, and Organization/Person entities with sameAs. Returns its own AEO score, a per-bot `crawlers` table and findings with rule ids (aeo.*). Provide one of `url` (one page, or a site with `crawl: true`), `html` or `dir` (build output). Set `aiBots: true` to also request the page with each AI bot's User-Agent and catch CDN or firewall blocks that robots.txt does not show.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL to audit (the start URL with `crawl`).

html.description: Raw HTML to audit instead of fetching a URL. Page checks only: there is no site to read robots.txt or llms.txt from.

dir.description: Build output directory to audit, with the robots.txt and llms.txt in it.

baseUrl.description: With `html` or `dir`: the origin the HTML is served from (default http://localhost/).

crawl.description: With `url`: crawl internal links and audit every page.

aiBots.description: With `url`: request the page with each AI bot's User-Agent (from this machine, not the bots' IPs) to find CDN or firewall blocks.

maxPages.description: Crawl or directory: maximum pages to audit (default 25 for a crawl, 500 for a directory).

tools.name: seo_list_rules
tools.description: List every rule this tool can report, with id, category, typical severity, what it checks and the generic fix. Filter by category or look up one rule id to understand a finding.

category.description: Filter by category (title, meta, headings, canonical, indexing, document, social, images, links, international, structured-data, content, keyword, response, rendering, performance, site, aeo).
